processing: A bred tea plant cultivar rather than a finished tea, chiefly used for green tea, which is fixed and dried without oxidation.
harvest_season: Very early: around Wuhan buds stir in mid-February and one-bud-one-leaf picking starts in early March. The picking season can run to early November.
appearance_dry: As green tea, typical of downy early-spring Hubei greens; little is documented about this variety's finished leaf.
appearance_liquor: Pale yellow-green, as is typical of early-spring greens.
appearance_wet: Soft, green, tender shoots with a dense coat of down.
taste_profile: Little tasting detail is recorded for this cultivar alone; as with other early-spring greens, expect a fresh, light and gently sweet cup.

brewing.notes: General handling for an early-picked green tea: water well off the boil, and do not rush the temperature.

vintage_note: Rarely sold under its own name. Its appeal is its very early spring picking, so leaf from it reaches the market early as a current-year green tea, usually at a premium over later pickings, as is common for the class.
description:
Echa No. 5 is a very early shrub cultivar from the Fruit and Tea Institute of the Hubei Academy of Agricultural Sciences, made by selection breeding. It matters to growers because it gets to market first: around Wuhan the first buds and leaves can be picked in early March.

The plant has medium-sized, oval, glossy green leaves that fold slightly inward, and shoots with dense down. It branches freely, buds densely and evenly, and stays tender for a long time. 100 one-bud-three-leaf shoots weigh 50 to 60 g.

The spring one-bud-two-leaf sample has about 2.4% amino acids, 28.3% polyphenols and 4.2% caffeine, so it is not a low-caffeine leaf. Tasting notes for this cultivar alone are few, and like other early-spring greens it should be brewed gently.

It is planted in Yingshan, Xianning and Xiaogan in Hubei, and recommended for tea areas on both sides of the Yangtze. You will mostly drink it without knowing, inside an early-season Hubei green.
history: Echa No. 5 passed Hubei's provincial variety review in 2002 under the number 鄂审茶001-2002, and later gained national recognition under the number 国品鉴茶2010018. A green tea called Bixue Yingchun made from its leaf is reported to have won a silver award at an international famous-tea contest in 2000.
